question.problem:
Given that the random variable $X$ has the probability density function

$$
f(x)=2{e}^{-|4x|},\,x\in (-\infty ,\infty ),
$$

its cumulative distribution function is

$$
F(x)={\begin{aligned}\frac{{e}^{4x}}{2},\, & x\le 0 \\ h(x),\, & x>0\end{aligned}
$$

where $h(x)=${{field-1}}.
question.worked_solution:
Since our random variable $X$ has a probability distribution function $f(x)$ that involves an absolute value, the cumulative distribution function takes the following form:

$$
F(x)=P(X\le x)={\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-\infty }^{x}2{e}^{4t}\,\text{d}t, & x\le 0 \\ {\int }_{-\infty }^{0}2{e}^{4t}\,\text{d}t+{\int }_{0}^{x}2{e}^{-4t}\,\text{d}t, & x>0\end{aligned}
$$

Let's compute the integrals. 

- If $x\le 0,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-\infty }^{x}2{e}^{4t}\,\text{d}t & ={\frac{{e}^{4t}}{2}|}_{-\infty }^{x} \\  & =\frac{{e}^{4x}}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

In particular, 

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-\infty }^{0}2{e}^{4t}\,\text{d}t & ={\frac{{e}^{4x}}{2}|}_{x=0} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

- If $x>0,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{x}2{e}^{-4t}\,\text{d}t & =-{\frac{{e}^{-4t}}{2}|}_{0}^{x} \\  & =-\frac{{e}^{-4x}}{2}+\frac{1}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

As a result, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-\infty }^{0}2{e}^{4t}\,\text{d}t+{\int }_{0}^{x}2{e}^{-4t}\,\text{d}t & =\frac{1}{2}+(-\frac{{e}^{-4x}}{2}+\frac{1}{2}) \\  & =1-\frac{{e}^{-4x}}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

So, the cumulative distribution function is given by

$$
F(x)={\begin{aligned}\frac{{e}^{4x}}{2},\, & x\le 0, \\ 1-\frac{{e}^{-4x}}{2},\, & x>0.\end{aligned}
$$
